topTasks.statement: Establish vegetation monitoring plots to protocol and record species composition, cover and density within the program's measurement-quality objectives
Identify plants on sample plots to the protocol's required taxonomic level, collecting labelled vouchers for any plant not identified with certainty
Conduct point-count, transect or call-playback wildlife surveys to protocol, recording detections, distance bands and survey conditions
Identify wildlife sign such as tracks, scat, nests and feeding remains to species or group, recording a confidence level for each record
Deploy camera traps and acoustic recorders at survey stations to the protocol's height, orientation and settings, recording station metadata
Measure temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity and turbidity in place with field meters calibrated before use and checked afterward
Collect grab water samples at locations and depths that represent the condition of interest, recording flow and site conditions at collection
Collect benthic macroinvertebrate, algae or fish community samples from a stream reach following the program's habitat-allocation protocol
Describe a soil profile's horizons, colour, texture, structure and coarse fragments in standard terminology on the program's description form
Collect soil samples at specified depths and locations for laboratory analysis of texture, nutrients, carbon or contaminants
Identify regional plants and animals to species with dichotomous keys and diagnostic features, collecting evidence for any record not identified with certainty
Accept, correct or reject AI-suggested species identifications against the specimen, image or recording, recording the diagnostic reason for each change

topTasks.statement: Install native plantings and seedings to the treatment specification, selecting microsites and handling stock so that it survives transplanting
Build low-tech process-based structures such as beaver dam analogues or post-assisted log structures, placing each from field reading of flow and channel form
Operate seed drills, tree planters or mulch blowers to the treatment specification, calibrating application rates before each unit
Build wildlife habitat features such as brush piles, nest structures and pollinator plantings to the design specification for the target species
Treat invasive plants by mechanical, chemical or biological methods to the treatment prescription, protecting non-target vegetation and water
Survey high-risk pathways such as trailheads, boat launches and road corridors for new invasive species, recording absences as well as detections
Install check dams, wattles or silt fences to the specification, keying and anchoring each so that flow cannot undercut or bypass it
Inspect erosion controls after storm events, repairing or redesigning any that failed and recording the failure mode
Construct trail tread to the design grade, outslope and width from a flagged alignment, reading soils and drainage along the segment
Maintain existing trails by clearing drainage structures, brushing corridors and repairing tread before damage spreads
Build rock structures such as steps, retaining walls or armored crossings to the specification, selecting and setting stone found on site
Use hand tools such as grubbing hoes, axes, crosscut saws and shovels for vegetation, trail and restoration work with safe spacing and body position
